subject: Physics
prompt: Newton's 2nd law in vector form
explain: Net force equals mass times acceleration; direction of F⃗ same as a⃗.

subject: Physics
prompt: Impulse equals change in
explain: Impulse J = F·Δt = Δp; it measures change in linear momentum.

subject: Physics
prompt: SI unit of linear momentum
explain: p = mv; units are kg·m/s, equivalent to N·s.

subject: Physics
prompt: Which law states 'every action has equal & opposite reaction'?
explain: 3rd law: F₁₂ = −F₂₁; action-reaction forces act on DIFFERENT bodies.

subject: Physics
prompt: Static friction max value formula
explain: Maximum static friction = μₛN; kinetic friction = μₖN (μₛ > μₖ always).

subject: Physics
prompt: Kinetic friction vs static friction: which is greater?
explain: μₛ > μₖ always; maximum static friction exceeds kinetic friction.

subject: Physics
prompt: Acceleration of system: two blocks m₁, m₂ on frictionless surface, force F
explain: Total mass resists force; a = F/(m₁+m₂) by Newton's 2nd law.

subject: Physics
prompt: Tension in string connecting m₁ & m₂ (force F on m₁ side)
explain: T pulls m₂ alone: T = m₂·a = m₂·F/(m₁+m₂).

subject: Physics
prompt: Acceleration of Atwood machine (m₁ > m₂, frictionless pulley)
explain: Net force = (m₁−m₂)g; total mass = m₁+m₂; so a = (m₁−m₂)g/(m₁+m₂).

subject: Physics
prompt: Normal force on a body in a lift accelerating upward
explain: Lift accelerates up: N−mg = ma, so N = m(g+a); apparent weight increases.

subject: Physics
prompt: Apparent weight in freely falling lift
explain: Free fall: a = g downward; N = m(g−g) = 0; apparent weightlessness.

subject: Physics
prompt: Law of conservation of momentum applies when
explain: Total momentum conserved only when net external force on system is zero.

subject: Physics
prompt: Angle of friction λ is related to μ by
explain: Angle of friction λ: tan λ = f/N = μN/N = μ.

subject: Physics
prompt: Angle of repose θᵣ for a block on incline
explain: At repose, mg sinθ = μₛ mg cosθ, so tan θᵣ = μₛ.

subject: Physics
prompt: Inertia of a body depends on its
explain: Inertia is the tendency to resist change in motion; it depends only on mass.

subject: Physics
prompt: Newton's 1st law is also called
explain: 1st law defines inertia: body stays at rest/uniform motion unless acted upon by force.

subject: Physics
prompt: Pseudo force magnitude on mass m in non-inertial frame (acceleration A)
explain: Pseudo force = mA directed opposite to the acceleration of the non-inertial frame.

subject: Physics
prompt: For block on frictionless incline (angle θ), acceleration along incline
explain: Component of gravity along incline = mg sinθ; a = g sinθ.

subject: Physics
prompt: Normal force on block on incline (angle θ)
explain: Perpendicular equilibrium on incline: N = mg cosθ.

subject: Physics
prompt: Action-reaction forces act on
explain: Newton's 3rd law: action and reaction always act on two DIFFERENT bodies.

subject: Physics
prompt: Friction force on a stationary block on a surface with no applied force
explain: Static friction is self-adjusting; with no applied force, friction = 0.

subject: Physics
prompt: Dimension of impulse
explain: Impulse = Δp = mv; dimensions = MLT⁻¹, same as momentum.

subject: Physics
prompt: For two blocks in contact on frictionless surface, contact force between them
explain: Contact force on m₂ = m₂·a = m₂·F/(m₁+m₂); force applied on m₁ side.

subject: Physics
prompt: Rolling friction is ___ compared to sliding (kinetic) friction
explain: Rolling friction << sliding friction; that's why wheels are used.

subject: Physics
prompt: For equilibrium of concurrent forces, Lami's theorem states
explain: Lami's theorem: each force divided by sine of opposite angle is constant for 3 concurrent forces.

subject: Physics
prompt: Limiting friction is independent of:
explain: Limiting static friction depends on N and μₛ, NOT on area of contact.

subject: Physics
prompt: A body moves with constant velocity. Net force on it is:
explain: Constant velocity ⟹ zero acceleration ⟹ net force = 0 (Newton's 1st law).

subject: Physics
prompt: Tension in string of Atwood machine (m₁>m₂):
explain: Standard Atwood result: T = 2m₁m₂g/(m₁+m₂).

subject: Physics
prompt: Normal force on mass m in a lift decelerating while moving upward:
explain: Deceleration upward means net acceleration is downward ⟹ N = m(g−a).

subject: Physics
prompt: A block rests on a rough incline. Which force balances the gravitational component along the incline?
explain: Static friction acts up the incline to balance mg sinθ when block is at rest.

subject: Physics
prompt: Coefficient of friction μ = tan θ corresponds to which condition?
explain: At angle of repose, block just starts sliding: μ = tan θᵣ.

subject: Physics
prompt: A 10 N force acts on a body for 3 s then stops. Which quantity changes by 30 N·s?
explain: Impulse J = FΔt = change in momentum; J = 10×3 = 30 N·s.

subject: Physics
prompt: Two equal masses collide and stick together. Speed of combined mass (initial speed u of one, other at rest):
explain: By conservation of momentum: mu = 2m·v ⟹ v = u/2.

subject: Physics
prompt: Friction between two surfaces is zero if:
explain: Friction exists only if μ ≠ 0; perfectly smooth surfaces means μ = 0 ⟹ f = 0.

subject: Physics
prompt: A horse pulls a cart. By Newton's 3rd law, cart pulls horse equally. Why does the system move?
options: Net external force on system is non-zero
explain: Action-reaction act on different bodies; ground friction on horse provides net external force.

subject: Physics
prompt: For a block on a rough surface, kinetic friction force direction is:
explain: Kinetic friction always opposes the direction of relative motion of the block.

subject: Physics
prompt: Which of these is NOT a contact force?
explain: Gravity acts at a distance (non-contact); normal, friction, tension are contact forces.

subject: Physics
prompt: A block of mass m on a frictionless surface connected via string over pulley to hanging mass M. Acceleration:
explain: Only M drives the system; total mass = M+m ⟹ a = Mg/(M+m).

subject: Physics
prompt: Centripetal force on mass m moving in circle (radius r, speed v) is provided by:
explain: Any net inward force (friction, tension, etc.) acts as centripetal force = mv²/r.

subject: Physics
prompt: Maximum speed of a car on a level circular road (radius r, μ, g):
explain: Friction provides centripetal force: μmg = mv²/r ⟹ v_max = √(μrg).

subject: Physics
prompt: Banking angle θ for ideal (frictionless) circular road of radius r at speed v:
explain: On banked road: N sinθ = mv²/r, N cosθ = mg ⟹ tan θ = v²/rg.

subject: Physics
prompt: A passenger in a turning car feels thrown outward. This is due to:
explain: In the rotating (non-inertial) frame, pseudo centrifugal force acts outward.

subject: Physics
prompt: If net force on a system of particles is zero, which is conserved?
explain: Zero net external force ⟹ dp/dt = 0 ⟹ total linear momentum is conserved.

subject: Physics
prompt: A spring balance shows less reading when in a downward-accelerating lift. The reduction equals:
explain: Apparent weight = m(g−a); reduction from true weight mg is ma.

subject: Physics
prompt: For a body in equilibrium on a rough incline, max angle before sliding is equal to:
explain: Angle of repose equals angle of friction λ = arctan(μ); body slides beyond this.

subject: Physics
prompt: Newton's 2nd law F = ma is valid only in:
explain: F = ma holds in inertial frames; pseudo forces must be added in non-inertial frames.

subject: Physics
prompt: A block is pushed against a wall by horizontal force F. Friction on block acts:
explain: Friction acts upward to balance gravity when block is pressed against vertical wall.

subject: Physics
prompt: The net force on a body is doubled while mass is halved. New acceleration becomes:
explain: a' = 2F/(m/2) = 4F/m = 4a; acceleration becomes 4 times.

subject: Physics
prompt: A man of mass m stands on a weighing scale in a lift moving up at constant speed. Reading is:
explain: Constant speed means zero acceleration; net force = 0, so normal force = mg.

subject: Physics
prompt: Which quantity remains unchanged when a constant force acts on a body for time t?
explain: Force changes velocity, momentum, and acceleration; mass is intrinsic and unchanged by applied force.
